items.title: David N. Baker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: So I feel that my books, Jerry Coker’s books, George Russell’s book, [and] Jamey Aebersold’s play-alongs have laid pretty much the foundation for jazz education. A lot of people don’t know this or don’t choose to acknowledge it, but when I go places, I think the people that I really respect are very aware of that foundation and that they’re going to my books. For a long time I would check attributions, and I would see, in book after book, my books being listed as source material. Dissertations – it’s almost…

I try to give credit always when I use material, and I’m always upset when I don’t see that credit. I’m always very suspicious when I see a book that doesn’t have an index, because it tells me that somebody didn’t take the time . . .
